clue.text: Ingenious engineers on the job, taking clubs to the fore

indicators.note: taking the card suit and carrying it elsewhere signals a letter being shifted within the word
to the fore says the shifted letter ends up at the very front of the assembly

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
someone on the job is working, i.e. active
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: Clever engineers at work bring golf clubs along to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + ACTIVE gives REACTIVE; 'taking clubs to the fore' moves its C to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenious person is inventive and original, the core sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Ran round judicial centre bearing mace, perhaps

indicators.note: round says the word for ran goes around the other piece

parts.note: to speed is to run fast, so ran gives sped

indicators.note: centre picks out the middle letters of the word judicial

explanation.surface: A man ran around the courthouse carrying a ceremonial mace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mace' is not the ceremonial staff but the spice from nutmeg husks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mace is a spice made from nutmeg husk, so food containing it is flavoured with spice.

clue.text: In time the French rejected fine ruler's novel logic

parts.note: in time means eventually, later

indicators.note: rejected means the French article is sent back, read the other way

parts.note: la is the French feminine form of the
fine as in a fine thread means thin
a king is a ruler; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Eventually French logic was dismissed as an unusual idea from a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: LA turned back gives AL, joining LATER to make LATERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking is an inventive, unconventional approach to solving problems, a fresh kind of reasoning.

clue.text: Host to arrive with agent coming back in

indicators.note: in places the reversed agent inside the word for arrive

parts.note: to come is to arrive

indicators.note: coming back reverses the short word for an agent

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A host is due to turn up with an agent returning inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere is the presenter or host of a show who introduces the acts.

clue.text: Small soft fish scale, say, reflecting the light

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A small soft fish has a scale that catches the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' is a verb here, ANGLE, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A spangle is a small shiny disc sewn on clothes, like a glittering scale.

clue.text: Fresh words of abuse male released behind lady's back

indicators.note: behind says the trimmed piece comes after the letter from the lady
a lady's back is the last letter of that word

parts.note: lady is taken as the word whose end is used

indicators.note: released means the letter for male is let go from the word

parts.note: giving someone a mouthful is hurling abuse at them

explanation.surface: A man spews abuse and is then freed, standing behind a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: MOUTHFUL without M is OUTHFUL, placed behind Y, the last letter of LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean young and vigorous, which is the sense of looking youthful.

clue.text: See record company that's popular and buy it!

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to buy it is slang for being killed, i.e. to die

explanation.surface: An advert telling you to check out a fashionable label and buy its records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buy it' is not shopping but the slang for meeting your end.
explanation.definitionFit: An indie is an independent record label, outside the major companies.

clue.text: Possibly counts bugs, having removed stone

indicators.note: having removed means the abbreviation for stone is taken out of the word

parts.note: to bug someone is to pester them
ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Somebody tallies up insects after getting rid of a pebble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counts' looks like a verb about tallying; it is the noblemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Counts are members of the nobility, and nobles of that rank are examples of the titled class.

clue.text: Bird, left-winger's floozie?

parts.note: a red is a left-winger, a communist; the 's adds an S
tart is slang for a floozie, a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: Asks which bird is the girlfriend of a leftist politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a red tail.

clue.text: Philistine in trouble over stabbing invader long ago

indicators.note: stabbing says the reversed trouble pierces the word for an invader

parts.note: the Goths were Germanic tribes who invaded the Roman Empire

indicators.note: over reverses the word for trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: An uncultured man is in trouble after a sword-thrust at an ancient raider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns the trouble word round; 'Philistine' looks like a word for a boor, but is the Biblical giant's people.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant slain by David in the Bible was a warrior of the Philistine people.

clue.text: Standard tale lacking force? Hopefully not

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
being not lacking in force or power is being capable

explanation.surface: A story told without force, though the teller hopes it isn't so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking force? Hopefully not' asks for the opposite of feeble: ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short story told to illustrate a moral lesson.

clue.text: Neaten up metal — it needs recasting, like this across clue

indicators.note: recasting means remoulding, so the letters are melted down and set in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy up metal that needs to be poured again.
explanation.walkthrough: Across clues run 26, 27, 28, so this one is third from last.
explanation.definitionFit: This clue is the third-last across clue, and third from last is the meaning of the word.

clue.text: 500 lines on paper variously composed

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, puts the newspaper first with the other pieces after it

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
D is the Roman numeral for 500
RY is the abbreviation for railway, i.e. lines

explanation.surface: Five hundred lines written on paper in different ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' are railway lines, RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundry means various or miscellaneous, things of mixed makeup.

clue.text: Old sections of bible that man had accepted precisely

indicators.note: accepted means the contraction is taken in among the other letters

parts.note: NT and OT are the New and Old Testaments
he'd is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: Ancient parts of scripture a man had taken on exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accepted' takes the contraction inside the old letter and the two Testaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving precisely on time is arriving punctually at the very moment.

clue.text: All library's items covered originally in firm cloth

indicators.note: in says the initials sit inside the abbreviation for a firm

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Everything in a library is bound in sturdy fabric from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials A, L, I, C go inside CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton fabric.

clue.text: On impulse kiss with speed before embracing

indicators.note: embracing says the word for before hugs the other pieces

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter
tempo is speed, especially of music

explanation.surface: Someone kisses quickly on a whim before hugging.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means spontaneous and unrehearsed, done without preparation.

clue.text: How flat may be made available, housing queen in flood

indicators.note: housing says one piece holds the other inside, like a building

parts.words: How flat may be made available
parts.note: a flat may be let out, or made available to rent
R is short for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A rented flat with a queen in residence is swamped by water.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rush of water, a deluge.

clue.text: Regulator stopping medieval vehicle

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the answer sits across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone controlling traffic halts an old cart from the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A valve is a device that regulates the flow of a fluid.

clue.text: A continental dig in irrational language

indicators.note: in places the other pieces inside the irrational number

parts.note: pi is an irrational number
un is French for a
a jab is a dig or poke

explanation.surface: A European takes an unreasonable poke at somebody's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' is not an adjective about the dig; it names a number that cannot be written as a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjabi is the language spoken in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Keep up close pursuit, gangster having escaped

indicators.note: having escaped means the gangster's name is gone from the word

parts.note: a calling is one's vocation or pursuit
Al Capone was the famous gangster

explanation.surface: Someone stays in hot pursuit after a mobster gets away.
explanation.walkthrough: CALLING without AL leaves CLING.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to grip tightly and stay attached to something.

clue.text: Poor quality lines turn up in ledger, surprisingly

indicators.note: in places the reversed turn inside the shuffled word
surprisingly hints the letters of ledger appear in an unexpected order
up reverses the word in a down entry

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Bad verse appears in an account book, to everyone's shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' scrambles ledger to DGEREL, and 'up' turns the turn round so it sits after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is badly written, trivial verse.

clue.text: What ref did frequently brought up after game

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the card game

parts.note: whist is a card game
to lead is to bring, so brought up gives led

explanation.surface: Soccer referee blew often after a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the referee blowing his whistle again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee repeatedly blew a whistle to stop play.

clue.text: Distant object, an item of little value

parts.note: distant means far
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: A remote object is something not worth much.
explanation.walkthrough: A FARTHING was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The coin was so small it became a byword for something worthless.

clue.text: Boozer's aim, maybe is to shoot council

parts.note: to dart is to shoot or move swiftly
a board is a council or committee

explanation.surface: A drinker's goal is to fire off at the local committee.
explanation.walkthrough: A boozer is a British pub, where darts is a traditional game.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub-goer playing darts aims at the target on the wall.

clue.text: Traveller recalled short girl — this could bring them closer

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read in reverse
short cuts the last letter off the word for traveller

parts.note: a gypsy is a traveller
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A traveller remembered a small girl.
explanation.walkthrough: GYPSY cut short is GYPS; reversed it is SPYG. 'Them' refers back to the traveller and girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A small telescope makes distant things look nearer.

clue.text: Suddenly bite through edible fish

parts.note: to snap is to bite suddenly
per means by or through

explanation.surface: A tasty fish bites suddenly through the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapper is a warm-water fish prized for eating.

clue.text: Spot rather like a mountain lake?

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
the suffix -ish means rather like

explanation.surface: Asks whether a blemish resembles a small lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to stain or sully.

clue.text: Go over blemish

definitions.meaning: to change sides, abandoning one's country

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to desert to the other side; the noun means a fault.

clue.text: Reveal bill local leader's raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a note is a bill, a banknote

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of local

explanation.surface: An announcement that a pub's top person put up a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: NOTE + L reads upwards as LETON.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is to disclose or admit something.

clue.text: Current supporter regularly pays half of capital

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of pays
half of keeps only the first three of the capital's six letters

parts.note: London is the British capital

explanation.surface: A capital city pays out, half of it at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of PAYS give PY; LONDON halved is LON.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tower holding up electricity cables.
